 Choose GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday productivity, document creation, coding assistance, and high-volume agent workflows.

GPT-6.2 is OpenAI’s model generation featuring Astra and Sol. Astra focuses on complex professional work, while Sol targets everyday productivity and coding.

## The gap is 4×, even after cache [...] This is evidence about visual frontend preference within those tasks. The intervals overlap, so the point estimates do not establish a decisive general win. Astra is worth including when the deliverable is an interactive scene whose rendered quality matters; review the actual output before paying its rate for all frontend work.

Both AA results above use snapshots accessed on 18 November 2026, approximately 02:30–02:40 UTC. No inference was run for this article. [...] Artificial Analysis's FrontierCode-AA 2.0 supplies a separate independent result: Astra max 45.38%; Sol max 44.38%. AA uses its own Stirrup harness on 132 private repository tasks, with three runs per task. That is a 1.00-percentage-point gap in a different setup, not a reproduction of OpenAI's scores or costs.

results.content:
On supported consumer plans, new Work chats default to Sol at Light reasoning effort. Enterprise workspaces with model access default to Sol at Medium. If you see the Power slider, open Advanced to choose a model and reasoning effort.

### Codex

In the Codex app and CLI, choose Astra to trace a bug across services, fix it, and test the affected workflows. Choose Sol to review a pull request or revise code in response to feedback. Use the model picker in the app or `/model` in the CLI. [...] # GPT-6.2

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API. Choose Astra for your hardest projects or Sol for everyday coding and writing.

## What’s new

### ChatGPT Work

Use Astra or Sol in Work on the web, desktop, or mobile with Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu. Enterprise and Edu admins must first enable the models in workspace settings. [...] ### Responses API

Use `gpt-6.2-astra` or `gpt-6.2-sol` in the Responses API. Both models support Ultrafast at launch.

In standard, single-agent mode, you can change reasoning effort or switch from plain text to structured output between replies. Append a `configuration_update` item before the next user message and keep the request-level settings unchanged. Keeping earlier input intact helps preserve reasoning across turns and keeps that input eligible for prompt caching.

results.content: Additionally, the company says GPT-6.1 Sol is more up front about its limitations and more reliable when it comes to honoring user intent and safety constraints.
